characters.name: Borges
characters.description: Wry librarian; asks what the measurements mean.

characters.name: Agnolo
characters.description: Dry accountant, through the radio; insists on actual costs.

characters.name: The Unspoken Orchestra
characters.description: Non-speaking musical ensemble; authored instrumental cues.

scenes.title: COLD OPEN — EVERYONE HAS A SCORE
scenes.setting: Future Radio studio; imagined soundscape as specified in source.
scenes.purpose: Reference-script benchmark; preserve dialogue and stage directions.

events.direction: A stadium crowd. Thousands of voices cheering. A scoreboard buzzes. An enormous mechanical counter advances.
Applause. A bell rings. More applause.

events.text: Quite possible. One measures mathematics. Another measures code. Another measures whether the machine knows which strawberry is larger.
And who measures the people measuring the strawberries?
Nobody. That would require another benchmark.

events.direction: THE UNSPOKEN ORCHESTRA strikes a single uncertain note.

scenes.title: SCENE ONE — THE COMMITTEE
scenes.setting: Future Radio studio; imagined soundscape as specified in source.
scenes.purpose: Reference-script benchmark; preserve dialogue and stage directions.

events.direction: A table unfolds. Three chairs scrape across the floor. A fourth chair appears, unoccupied.

events.text: I propose a test of literary comprehension.
What about something valuable that hasn't earned money yet?
What if we tested all three?
Which would be entirely consistent with the rest of the industry.

events.direction: THE ORCHESTRA plays a triumphant fanfare. It immediately collapses.

scenes.title: SCENE TWO — THE MISSING MEASUREMENT
scenes.setting: Future Radio studio; imagined soundscape as specified in source.
scenes.purpose: Reference-script benchmark; preserve dialogue and stage directions.

events.text: Wait. What are we actually trying to do?
We don't know what it costs to make the show.
I have been saying that for weeks.
You keep telling us what we've spent.
Every episode is different. Different scripts. Different models. Different voices. Different production processes.
And we're learning things every time. But we can't compare the results.
Because we have no standard unit.
Everything we need to know to make the next one better.

scenes.title: SCENE THREE — WHAT DOES AN EPISODE COST?
scenes.setting: Future Radio studio; imagined soundscape as specified in source.
scenes.purpose: Reference-script benchmark; preserve dialogue and stage directions.

events.direction: Agnolo opens an enormous ledger. Pages turn faster and faster.

events.text: Very well. Let us begin. What does an episode require?
Accounting is not the enemy of art, Leonardo.

events.direction: The Orchestra introduces a rhythm. Agnolo's percussion ticks like a metronome.

events.text: Here's what I want to know. If somebody has a machine, and an hour, and an idea, can they make an episode?

scenes.title: SCENE FOUR — THE MINER
scenes.setting: Future Radio studio; imagined soundscape as specified in source.
scenes.purpose: Reference-script benchmark; preserve dialogue and stage directions.

events.direction: A faint mechanical hum, almost lost beneath the orchestra.

events.text: There's still the matter of paying for it.
What if someone else generated it?
That's not the same as free.
I didn't say free. I said someone else.
There's a system called Hashference. You can pay for inference with computational work.
A machine thinking in exchange for another machine working.
And then we ask other people to run the same experiment.
Or different models. Different tools. Different approaches.
What prevents them from making terrible episodes?
An enormous quantity of terrible episodes.
Maybe. But think about what happens if somebody makes a good one for a tenth of what ours costs.
And somebody else makes one for a tenth of that.

events.direction: The mechanical hum grows. A mining fan spins up.
The Orchestra picks up the hum and turns it into a sustained note.

scenes.title: SCENE FIVE — AN EPISODE MUST DO SOMETHING
scenes.setting: Future Radio studio; imagined soundscape as specified in source.
scenes.purpose: Reference-script benchmark; preserve dialogue and stage directions.

events.text: A cheap episode need not be an interesting episode.
An interesting episode need not be a useful episode.
And a useful episode may be extraordinarily expensive.
Perhaps it must persuade someone to read a book.
Or convince somebody to make another episode.
Because a successful episode could produce its own successor.
And the successor could improve the process.
And the next one learns from both.
A radio show that makes itself!

events.direction: The Orchestra starts a glorious crescendo.

events.text: We still have to make the first one.

scenes.title: SCENE SIX — THE BENCHMARK
scenes.setting: Future Radio studio; imagined soundscape as specified in source.
scenes.purpose: Reference-script benchmark; preserve dialogue and stage directions.

events.text: I believe we've entered a loop.
How much time do we have?
Until the end of next week.
Fine. We establish a baseline first, then try to beat it.
The episode exists. We know what it cost. We publish it. And at least one person tries to make a better one.
Cheaper. Faster. More interesting. More people watching. More people participating.
Different people will choose different approaches.
We record them all. We compare what can be compared.
A benchmark with an open future.
Finally, a benchmark with proper accounting.

scenes.title: SCENE SEVEN — THE INVITATION
scenes.setting: Future Radio studio; imagined soundscape as specified in source.
scenes.purpose: Reference-script benchmark; preserve dialogue and stage directions.

events.direction: The Orchestra begins playing the opening theme again, but this time the arrangement is simpler. Fewer instruments. The same melody.

events.text: There's something else we haven't accounted for.
They've been listening to us design a benchmark.
But now they know the rules.
They would need the character instructions.
And somewhere to submit their work.
It asks how much an episode costs.
As soon as this episode finishes generating.
Then we have a better benchmark.
Then we have our first result.
And if someone makes something we never imagined?

events.direction: THE UNSPOKEN ORCHESTRA plays the theme one final time. Its last note resolves into the low hum of the miner.

scenes.title: POST-CREDITS — THE RECEIPT
scenes.setting: Future Radio studio; imagined soundscape as specified in source.
scenes.purpose: Reference-script benchmark; preserve dialogue and stage directions.

events.direction: An old printer begins feeding paper.

events.text: Whether we're counting the time spent arguing about the benchmark.
Oh, we're going to need a bigger ledger.
